option_b: The increase in accuracy of position fixes is independent of the receiver position in relation to a D-GPS ground station
option_c: A D-GPS receiver can detect and correct for SA providing a more accurate position fix
option_d: Only D-GPS allows position fixes accurate enough for 'Non Precision Approaches'

question_text: How does a receiver of the NAVSTAR/GPS satellite navigation system determine the elevation and azimuth data of a satellite relative to the location of the antenna?
option_a: It calculates it by using Almanac data transmitted by the satellites
option_b: The data is stored in the receiver together with the Pseudo Random Noise (PRN) code
option_c: The data is based on the direction to the satellite determined at the location of the antenna
option_d: The data is determined by the satellite and transmitted together with the navigation message

question_text: In relation to the NAVSTAR/GPS satellite navigation system, 'Search the Sky' is a:
option_a: procedure that starts after switching on a receiver if there is no stored satellite data available
option_b: continuous process by the ground segment to monitor the GPS satellites
option_c: procedure performed by the receiver to recognise new satellites becoming operational
option_d: continuous procedure performed by the receiver that searches the sky for satellites rising above the horizon

question_text: What is the procedure to be followed if, on a flight under IFR conditions using the NAVSTAR/GPS satellite navigation system, the number of satellites required to maintain the RAIM (Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring) function are not available?
option_a: The flight may be continued using other certificated navigation systems
option_b: The flight has to be continued under VFR conditions
option_c: A constant heading and speed must be flown until the required number of satellites are again available
option_d: The flight may be continued as planned if at least 4 satellites are available and the pilot monitors the GPS-System manually

question_text: Which of the following, if any, is a prerequisite if a receiver of a NAVSTAR/GPS satellite navigation system is to be used in combination with a multi sensor system?
option_a: The prescribed IFR-equipment must be installed and operational
option_b: The prescribed IFR-equipment must be in working correctly and the navigation information continuously displayed
option_c: The RAIM-function of the GPS receiver must be able to monitor all prescribed navigation systems
option_d: Multi-sensor systems are not certificated for flights under IFR conditions

question_text: Which of the following procedures must be adopted if, on a flight under IFR conditions using a NAVSTAR/GPS satellite navigation system receiver, the position fix obtained from the GPS receiver differs from the position of conventional navigation systems by an unacceptable amount?
option_a: It may be continued using conventional navigation systems
option_b: It may be continued using NAVSTAR/GPS, prior to the next flight all systems must be checked
option_c: It must be continued under VFR conditions
option_d: The pilot must determine the reason for the deviation and correct the error or switch off the faulty system

question_text: What datum is used for the Minimum Descent Altitude (MDA) on a non-precision approach when using the NAVSTAR/GPS satellite navigation system?
option_b: If using Differential-GPS (D-GPS) the altitude obtained from the D-GPS, otherwise barometric altitude

question_text: Which of the following is the datum for altitude information when conducting flights under IFR conditions on airways using the NAVSTAR/GPS satellite navigation system?
option_b: The average of GPS altitude and barometric altitude
option_d: GPS altitude if 4 or more satellites are received otherwise barometric altitude
